senses.gloss: m. (Pers. dânkh; δανάκη) Danka, a small Persian coin, the sixth of a Denar, in gen. one sixth.
units: B. Mets. 60ᵇ מאה בד׳ one hundred P’rutah for a d.—
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 39b:6">Ib. 39ᵇ</cite> <he>ואידך תילתא יהבינן ד׳ וכ׳</he> and of the remaining one third we give one sixth to the sister, and for the other one sixth we appoint &c.—
Zeb. 48ᵃ; Kerith. 22ᵇ בת ד׳, בר ד׳ worth a d.—
<cite ref="Shabbat 35a">Sabb. 35ᵃ</cite> [read with Rashi:] <he>א״ב פלגא דד׳</he> the difference between two thirds and three fourths (of a mile) is half a sixth.—Pl. <he>דַּנְקֵי</he>.
<cite ref="Rosh Hashanah 26a:18">R. Hash. 26ᵃ</cite> (identified with <cite ref="M02070"><he>מְעָה</he></cite> a. <cite ref="S02246"><he>קְשִׂיטָה</he></cite>).
